title: Why the isovector O1 gets 1.3 sigma at delta = 0 while the isoscalar gets none: isospin, the M-response node and what isospin violation can buy
question: Why does LZ's elastic O1 receive 0 sigma for isoscalar but 0.8-1.3 sigma for isovector couplings at m >= 400 GeV; where is the isovector M-response node; how does the isovector spectrum at 248 keV differ from low energies; how far can general f_n/f_p (incl. xenophobic -0.7 and proton-only) reduce N_lo, and is any ratio compatible with a lone event (N_lo <= 3-5)?
headline_result: The isovector amplitude Z F_p - N F_n has its second M node at 182 keV (isotopes 173-190) instead of the isoscalar 267 keV, so at 248 keV isovector and isoscalar rates are equal at fixed c_p while the isovector low-energy rate is x0.022: N_lo falls 2753 -> 477 and P016's Z rises 0.48 -> 1.65 sigma, reproducing LZ's 0/1.3 sigma pattern as a node effect; scanning f_n/f_p, N_lo is minimal (7.3 at 1 TeV) at r = -0.744 and never reaches <= 5; for inelastic O1 only pure isovector puts 248 keV at the spectral peak (70th percentile), while the Higgsino is neutron-like (98.4th)
model_or_mechanism: O1 with general isospin ratio r = f_n/f_p via exact quadratic-form decomposition of WimPyDD shell-model spectra (c0 = c_p(1+r), c1 = c_p(1-r)); per-isotope M responses W_pp/W_nn/W_pn from DMFormFactor-v6 density matrices; P016 few-bin likelihood; delta = 300 keV percentiles
stance: neutral (tool, projection, or constraint) - removes O1v's apparent edge and closes the isospin-violation route for elastic SI
confidence: medium - exact within WimPyDD's responses; isovector shape near 248 keV is nuclear-structure fragile (LZ's 1.3 sigma implies ~2x WimPyDD's isovector N_lo)
